intro: Culinary Academy of India and Leo Academy both sit in Hyderabad, and this page compares their recorded BHM fees, placements, admission routes and campus setting, using our database and official pages we opened in 2026.

Culinary Academy of India vs Leo Academy is not a single winner. Culinary Academy of India is recorded as a private institute, while Leo Academy is public. Pick the campus that matches the programme you want, the fee you can pay, and the admission test you will take.

sections.heading: Culinary Academy of India vs Leo Academy for BHM: which is better in 2026
paragraphs: Choose Leo Academy if you want a public BHM option and the admission route and fees that usually come with a government or state university campus.
Choose Culinary Academy of India if a private campus, its specific specialisation or its recorded placement year fits your plan better, after you have checked the official fee notice.

Culinary Academy of India lists Bachelor of Catering Technology and Culinary Arts. Leo Academy lists Bachelor  in Hotel Management (BHM), Bachelor of Hotel Management & Catering Technology (BHMCT), Craftsmanship Course in Food Production.

sections.heading: Fees: what our records show, and what the official pages say
paragraphs: On this page we quote a programme total when we hold a Total Fees record, and we skip application, hostel-only or short-course rows so a registration fee is not treated as tuition.

Our records list ₹47,333 a year as tuition fees for Culinary Academy of India's Bachelor of Catering Technology and Culinary Arts. Treat that as a year figure, not a confirmed full-programme total, until you check the official notice.

Our records list ₹1 lakh a year as tuition fees for Leo Academy's Bachelor of Hotel Management & Catering Technology (BHMCT). Treat that as a year figure, not a confirmed full-programme total, until you check the official notice.
If fees are your only filter, confirm the current official circular for the exact programme and batch you will join, because year figures and older rows can understate the real cost.

sections.heading: Placements compared
paragraphs: In our records, Culinary Academy of India's 2023 figures are an average of ₹3 lakh and a highest of ₹8 lakh for Bachelor of Catering Technology and Culinary Arts. These are historical batch outcomes, not a salary promise.

In our records, Leo Academy's 2023 figures are an average of ₹6 lakh and a highest of ₹12 lakh for Bachelor of Hotel Management & Catering Technology (BHMCT). These are historical batch outcomes, not a salary promise.
If you are comparing offers, use the latest official placement report from each institute and match the programme name, not an executive or certificate batch.

sections.heading: Admission and eligibility
paragraphs: Culinary Academy of India's recorded admission tests on this page include NCHMCT JEE.
Leo Academy's recorded admission tests on this page include NCHMCT JEE.
Eligibility wording can change by cycle. Use the current official admission brochure rather than last year's cut-off stories.

sections.heading: Location and campus
paragraphs: Both campuses are in Hyderabad, Telangana. The choice is less about moving city and more about the programme, fees and admission route.
Visit both campuses if you can, or at least read the official hostel and location notes, before you accept an offer.

sections.heading: Verdict: who should pick which college
paragraphs: If you want the stronger recorded public standing or NIRF rank in this pair, Leo Academy is the safer first pick, after you have checked official fees and seats.
Culinary Academy of India can still be the better fit if its specialisation, city or recorded fee level matches what you can join this year.
If fees are the only filter, do not use the lowest number in our raw rows. Check each official fee notice for the exact programme and batch you will join.
